problem: Architects and engineers use decades old software and spend time on meeting minutes, RFIs, submittals and field reports.
product_category: AI tools for architecture, engineering and construction

founders.name: Alexander von Boetticher
education: Research in theoretical physics (plasma turbulence, magnetic confinement fusion) at Oxford; degrees not listed

technical_complexity.rationale: Early products were AI meeting notes and summaries on top of speech and language models; later construction document agents need integrations with Procore and Autodesk.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with project systems add lock-in, but meeting notes tools were widely copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Procore later added built-in AI features per a comparison page; dates not verified.

market_need_then: The company says AEC software is decades old and hard to use; the sources found give no dated demand figures.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B tone with a data privacy pledge that no models train on customer data

branding.community_and_virality: Publishes build week updates and a changelog; no third party community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning but no distinctive brand asset or outside press on the brand found.

pivots.from: General AI meeting notes and summaries (launched 2022 per one search summary of its changelog)
pivots.to: AI platform for architects, engineers and builders

outcome_analysis: Cogram began around 2021 with AI meeting notes and by 2025 sells a broader AEC platform with agents, RFIs and submittals, offices in several cities and 15 staff. No acquisition, shutdown or layoffs were found. Funding cannot be judged because only aggregators report a round and they conflict.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable and FundedIQ list a 4M USD seed in 2022-04 and 500K pre-seed in 2022-01; CB Insights shows 500K total; Soma Capital and Creative Destruction Lab appear as investors. No press release found, so no round is recorded. The Seedtable page returned 403. Pivot date and original product description come from a search summary and are only partly supported. Competitor list left empty: Newforma, Procore and Autodesk appear only in 2025 to 2026 pages, none dated at the batch. Headquarters conflicts across sources (New York per YC, Berlin per others). Completeness pass: both rounds rest on a single database (Seedtable, echoed by FundedIQ) with no press release or filing; CB Insights shows only 500K total, so the 4M seed is contested.
